newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia gets first woman president - for a day.
newsitem.headline: Colombia gets first woman president - for a day.

text.p: Foreign Relations Minister Maria Emma Mejia will become president of Colombia for a day when Enesto Samper travels to Guatemala on Dec. 29 -- the first time a woman has ever ruled the country.

Mejia will have the power to approve new laws and declare war on other countries as Samper and his right-hand man, Interior Minister Horacio Serpa, join other leaders and politicians in the Central American republic to witness the signing of a peace treaty between the Guatemalan government and the country's leftist rebels that will formally end 36 years of civil war.
Under the constitution, when both the president and the interior minister are away the reins of power pass to the foreign relations minister.
"Don't think I'm not a little hesitant about this," Mejia told reporters on Monday. "But after all I regard this as a tribute to all working women in Colombia."
The foreign relations minister was voted the country's second most popular woman after teenage pop star Shakira in a poll published by the respected El Espectador newspaper last week.
